title: registry-item.json — module descriptor
description: shadcn-shaped descriptor authored in the CLI/registry repo. The applier reads it off disk to resolve dependencies, apply files + npm deps + patches, and copy the module's skill folder(s) into .claude/skills/ (build spec §3.3).

when.description: Ship this entry only while the condition holds (#242, ADR 0054). The keys combine with AND: `testing` ships it only when the project's testing mode is not `off`, and `installed` only when every named module is in the resolved install set. A target whose entries it drops is skipped, not refused. It decides the first write only: an entry already in the manifest stays managed in every mode. Backfill writes the entry once the condition turns true.

testing.description: Ship only when testing.mode is `tests-after` or `tdd`. The one allowed value is `true`; leave the key out for an entry that ships in every mode.

installed.description: Ship only when every named module is installed. `remove` of a named module also removes the entry.

name.description: The imported binding, also its local name.

from.description: The module specifier, relative to the generated file (it sits beside the file that holds the table, so a specifier that worked there works here) or a package name.

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor validation.

name.description: Module name (lowercase, digits, hyphens). Unique within the registry.

type.description: `saasaloy:capability` scaffolds an app/package and establishes extension points; `saasaloy:feature` extends capabilities by dropping files into their conventions.

description.description: One line on what the module gives a project. `saasaloy list --json` prints it, so an agent can pick a module without reading its skill. Optional in the schema; `saasaloy doctor` on a registry fails a descriptor without it (#223).

stage.description: The product stage that usually earns this module: `validate` (landing page and waitlist), `mvp` (sign-in, admin, email), `teams` (organizations, tenancy, roles), `money` (subscription and payments) or `scale` (jobs, caching, files, rate limits, API access). A supporting module the README's stage table does not name takes the earliest stage of the modules that need it, and a provider or a driver takes its capability's stage.

needs.description: What the module needs outside the repo before it works in production: `cloudflare-paid` (a paid Workers plan), `stripe` (a Stripe account), `domain` (a domain onboarded by hand) or `vendor-account` (an account with another vendor). An empty array means nothing beyond the free tier.

requires.description: Tool versions this descriptor needs. A descriptor sets `additionalProperties: false`, so an old CLI meeting a new field already fails — as a raw schema dump, and not at all when an existing field merely changed meaning. Declaring a range turns both into one fatal, actionable message, checked before any write is planned. Optional: a descriptor without it works on every CLI version.

saasaloy.description: Semver range the running `saasaloy` CLI has to satisfy (e.g. `>=0.3`, `>=0.3 <2`, `^1.2.0`, `1.x`). Any range shape is accepted, upper bounds included, so there is no separate maximum field. A CLI outside the range refuses the whole run and names this module, even when it is a transitive `dependsOn`.

dependsOn.description: Modules this one requires. Resolved recursively and topologically sorted behind a confirmation prompt.

conflictsWith.description: Modules this one refuses to sit beside — two implementations of the same capability, say. `add` refuses with a message naming both modules when a conflicting module is already installed. Either side may declare it: the field is recorded into saasaloy-lock.json, so the refusal fires in either install order. Never auto-resolved; `add` uninstalls nothing.

requiresOneOf.description: Modules exactly one of which has to be present — a capability naming its mutually exclusive drivers or owners (e.g. `api-keys` naming `api-keys-organization` and `api-keys-user`, or `database` naming its one driver, `database-postgres`). `add` counts a module as present when it is already installed or arrives in the same resolved graph, refuses when none is, and offers the list as a prompt on an interactive terminal (#98, ADR 0026).

dependencies.description: npm packages merged into the consumer's `dependencies`. Each must be exact-pinned `name@version` (e.g. zod@4.0.5) — bare names and ranges are rejected; `pnpm deps:update` fills/refreshes the versions.

devDependencies.description: npm packages merged into the consumer's `devDependencies` (e.g. @types/*, build tooling). Same exact-pinned `name@version` form as `dependencies`. A name declared in both buckets lands in `dependencies` only.

files.description: Files to copy into the project. `path` is relative to the module folder; `target` resolves through the project's alias map.

path.description: Source path relative to the module folder (e.g. files/api/routes/waitlist.ts). No '.' or '..' path segment: the applier refuses one at runtime and this fails the descriptor at authoring time (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .gitignore is fine.

target.description: Alias-prefixed destination (e.g. @api/routes/waitlist.ts). No '.' or '..' path segment: the applier refuses one at runtime and this fails the descriptor at authoring time (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .gitignore is fine.

seed.description: Write this file once and hand it to the project (#310, ADR 0060). `add` and backfill write it and record it in the manifest with this module as owner. `saasaloy update` never overwrites or merges it, and puts it back only when it is missing from disk. `saasaloy remove` deletes it while its hash still matches the record, and keeps it with a warning once the project changed it. Use it for an extension point a managed file imports, so the project edits the seed file and the managed file stays clean.

untested.description: Why this file ships with no test beside it (#242). Reserved for a later descriptor guard (#243), which is to read the reason rather than fail the file.

envVars.description: Environment variables the module needs: NAME → human description (or default/placeholder).

envServices.description: Which services read each of this module's `envVars` — a service being a workspace that reads a `.env` (`api`, `web`, `admin`), or `deploy`, the Cloudflare credentials `pnpm deploy:production` loads with no file. `default` covers every key the module declares; a key named alongside it overrides that list for itself. `saasaloy add` groups the key list in `packages/env/.env.example` under a `# @services` line per distinct set. Omit it and the `PUBLIC_` prefix rule decides instead, with a warning naming the module: a prefixed key goes to every client service, everything else to the api.

envOptional.description: Keys from `envVars` that may stay empty. `saasaloy add` writes a `# Blank on purpose` line above each one in `packages/env/.env.example`, which is what stops `pnpm env:setup` failing on a key the capability's schema gives a default or marks optional. Every name here must also appear in `envVars`.

devVars.description: Local-development values for a subset of `envVars`: NAME → the value `saasaloy add` pre-fills into the generated `packages/env/.env.example`. Only for a value that is the same on every machine and is not a secret (a loopback URL, a fixed port). Every key here must also appear in `envVars`; a key absent here is written with an empty value for the owner to fill in.

removeWarnings.description: Warnings saved with an installed module and shown before removal. Use this for deployed resources that file and patch removal cannot delete safely.

patches.description: Structural config patches the render applies to a file another module or the base ships (issue #7). A flat array where each op names its own target `file` and codemod `kind` (wrangler.jsonc bindings, package.json dependency merges, package.json script entries, Drizzle columns, one const property); kind-specific payload fields are defined by the engine. A registration table is not a patch: it goes in `tables` and `entries`. An empty array means no patches (ADR 0019).

file.description: Project-relative POSIX path of the file to patch (e.g. apps/api/wrangler.jsonc). No leading slash or @alias, and no '.' or '..' path segment (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .eslintrc.json is fine.

kind.description: Which codemod applies this patch. The four table kinds of the old engine (`plugin-array`, `const-array`, `chained-route`, `nav-entry`) are gone: a module adds a row to a table with `entries`.

constName.description: Name of the module-scope const object that holds the property (e.g. deployConfig).

property.description: Top-level property to fill (e.g. ciWorkflow). The patch writes only while it reads `undefined`, so a value the owner set stays.

value.description: JSON value written in place of `undefined`. `remove` puts `undefined` back while the property still holds it.

name.description: Script key to upsert into the target's `scripts` map (e.g. db:generate).

value.description: Command the script runs (e.g. drizzle-kit generate). An entry already present under this key is never overwritten.

exportName.description: Exported binding holding the Drizzle table — the name in `export const <name> = sqliteTable("…", { … })`. The columns object is that call's second argument.

column.description: Property key added to the columns object (e.g. subscriptionCustomerId). Also the match key: a table already carrying it is left alone, whatever it holds, and `remove` finds the column by it.

value.description: The column expression, verbatim source (e.g. text("subscription_customer_id")). Written as-is and compared as-is on removal, so a column the user has since edited is refused rather than dropped. Ship one patch per dialect when the two builders differ.

import.description: Named import the value needs, dropped again on `remove` when nothing else references it. Omit it when the table's other columns already import the builder.

from.description: Module specifier to import from (e.g. drizzle-orm/sqlite-core).

tables.description: Registration tables this module owns (plan 0116, Phase 7). The render writes each table into its `file` in full on every run, class `generated`, sorted by each entry's `order` and then by module name. The file that holds the table imports the export and spreads it after the entries the module ships inline; the owner's own entries go after the spread.

id.description: Unique across the payload, `<owner>.<table>` such as `email.providers`. The generated file exports the table under the camelCase of the id: `email.providers` is `emailProviders`.

file.description: The generated file: a project path or an `@alias` path, named `<name>.generated.ts` beside the file that holds the table. Several tables may share one file.

shape.description: `calls` exports `[a(), b()]` (entries name `call` and `import`). `objects` exports `[{ … }]` (entries name `entry`). `routes` exports a function that chains `.route(path, router)` onto the Hono app it takes (entries name `path`, `call` and `import`). `nav` exports `[{ area, group, …entry, icon }] as const` (entries name `area`, `group`, `entry` and the icon as `import`).

type.description: `objects` only: the element type, imported as a type, so the export reads `T[]`.

entries.description: Rows this module adds to tables, its own or another module's (plan 0116, Phase 7). Which fields a row needs depends on the shape of its table; the render refuses a row that does not fit.

call.description: `calls`: the factory the table calls, printed `call()`. `routes`: the router, printed `.route(path, call)`.

import.description: `calls` and `routes`: the import of `call`. `nav`: the icon component, printed `icon: <name>`.

entry.description: `objects`: the JSON object of the row. `nav`: the row without its icon (`to`, `label`, `shortcut`, …).

area.description: `nav`: the `to` of the area the row goes into.

group.description: `nav`: the label of the group. A group the area does not have yet is added after its last group.

order.description: Sort key. Absent means 1000. A lower order comes first; equal orders sort by module name, and one module's rows keep their descriptor order.

scaffolds.description: New workspaces a capability module creates (apps/packages). Each entry births one workspace: copies its files to workspace-root-relative targets and registers the aliases it declares into saasaloy.json (ADR 0013).

workspace.description: New workspace directory, project-relative POSIX (e.g. apps/api). No leading slash or @alias.

aliases.description: Alias → path-prefix map this scaffold registers into saasaloy.json (e.g. { "@api": "apps/api/src" }).

additionalProperties.description: Project-relative path prefix (POSIX separators, no leading slash).

files.description: Files copied into the workspace. `path` is relative to the module folder; `target` is relative to the workspace root (no @alias — the alias root doesn't exist yet).

path.description: Source path relative to the module folder (e.g. files/src/index.ts). No '.' or '..' path segment: the applier refuses one at runtime and this fails the descriptor at authoring time (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .dev.vars.example is fine.

target.description: Destination relative to the workspace root (e.g. src/index.ts). No leading slash or @alias, and no '.' or '..' path segment (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .dev.vars.example is fine.

seed.description: Write this file once and hand it to the project (#310, ADR 0060). `add` and backfill write it and record it in the manifest with this module as owner. `saasaloy update` never overwrites or merges it, and puts it back only when it is missing from disk. `saasaloy remove` deletes it while its hash still matches the record, and keeps it with a warning once the project changed it. Use it for an extension point a managed file imports, so the project edits the seed file and the managed file stays clean.

enablesTesting.description: Adding this module turns testing on (#242, ADR 0054): on a project whose testing.mode is `off`, `add` plans with `tests-after`, saves it once the apply succeeds, and backfills every gated entry. It leaves `tdd` alone, and `remove` never changes the mode.

agent.description: AI context contributed by this module. A module ships skill folder(s) that `add` copies into .claude/skills/ (recorded in the manifest for a clean `remove`); it never edits the committed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.

skills.description: Skill folder(s) relative to the module folder, copied into .claude/skills/.
